YARE, is the Sea word for Nimble, Ready, Quick, or Expeditious. YAW ES. At Sea, they say a Ship makes Yavoes, when thro the fault of him at Helm Ihe is not kept steady in her Course, but makes Angles in and out; to prevent which, the Conner crys, steady, steady ; keep her Thus, Thus. YEAR -• The Time the Sun takes to go through the twelve Signs of the Zodiack. This is properly the Natural or Tropical Year, and contains 365 Days, 5 Hours, and 12 Minutes. The Sydereal Year, is that Time in which the Sun departing from any fixed Star, comes to it again ; and this is in 36 5 Days, 6 Hours, and almost , o Minutes. But according to Mr. Newton’ s New Theory of the Moon, the byderial Year is 365 D. 6 H. 9' 14'' j and the Tropical, 365 D. 5 H. 48' 57". The Civil Tear, which is commonly used by all Nations, is very various, both as to its Beginning, and also as to its Length, according as they follow the Course of the Sun, Moon, or both. The Civil Lunar Year contains la Lunations or Synodical Months, and contains but 354 Days: This being 11 Days less than the Solar Year, its Head in about 33 Years will run through all the Months and Seasons of the Year. This kind of Year is now used by that«, ^,and seems to have had its first Pise in Countiies where the difference between Summer and Winter is not so sensible as it is wirl) us ■, and where for want of Astronomy, ' they know not how to estimate the Solar Year and therefore began their Account of Months from the Phases of the Moon. And hence, as the learned Astronomer Dr. Gregory hints, it came so pass, that they began the Account of their Civil Day at Sun-set; for their Day must begin when their Month and Year did, and that was, with the New Moon; which being to be determin’d by view, could not be discover’d till after Sun-ser. The Jevos had their Secular Year, which began at the Autumnal Equinox ; and their Sacred Tear, which began at the Vernal one. The Egyptians, Caldeans, and Assyrians, first measured the Year by the Course of the Sun, which they supposed to contain but 360.Days; afterwards 5 more were added by Mercury, which he called incryoub'*', i. e. added ; but yet no notice was taken of the 6 Hours ; by which means, th? Egyptian Year hath no fixed Place in reference to the true Solar Year; bur anticipating a Day every four Years, runs quite round in 1460 Years. This way of Reckoning continued till Egypt becoming a Province of the Roman Empire, they took the Julian. Account, only they kept the Names of their Months still, and ordered the matter so, that their That, the first Day of the Year, always happen’d on the 29th of August in the Julian's ear. So that the Egyptian or Coptick Year is, 4 Months and 3 Days before the Roman Year, which begins with the Calends of January. The Persians Account (according to the Egyptian way J 36; Days. The Arabs, Saracens, and Turks , count their Year by the morion of the Moon, and make it consist of 12 Moons or Months, whereof some have 30, and some 29 Days alternately ; and these altogether make but 354 Days ; so that their Month Muharran, in which they place the beginning of the Year, in less than 34 Years will run quire round, and be in all Scalons. The Arabs indeed, by a Cycle of 30 Years, do remedy this, by means of an Intercalation or Embolism of 11 Days. The Greeks counted their Year by the motion of both Sun and Moon, and finding that there was 11 Days difference between the Lunar and Solar Year; at first they added an Intercalary Month every two Years, containing 22 Days, which therefore they called iuGor/uYic, the added or inserted Month. Afterwards considering the 6 Hours also, they put their Embolism off till 4 Years end ; and then making the 3 first Years co contain 354 Days apiece, (which is the Lunar Year) this made the 4th Year to have 399 Days.And to make this Intercalation the more Remarkable, they instituted the Olympick. Games, on every such 4th Year; whence came the Computation by Olympiads ; each of which contained 4 Years. Nevertheless they found that this would not do, in process of Time; and therefore they first reduced the Intercalation to 8 and then to 1 1 Years ; but still there was great Confusion, till one Mete, a Citizen and famous Astronomer of Athens, thought of joining the two last Periods 8 and 1 x together ; which doing, he made a Period of 19 Years, in which the two motions of the Sun and Moon are wholly acccmmodstecl, am) the Moon changes on the

YEA Y O K the same Day of the Month that she did 19 Years before. This Discovery, for its Fullness, was much Celebrated, and the Number of the Period 19, the Athenians ordered to be set up in a publick Place, and to be written in C haracters of Gold ; whence it took the Name it still retains, being called the Golden Number. The Athenians began their Year at the New Moon after the Summer Solstice; in their Mouth Hecatombaton, as Plutarch says. There were also some Nations who made their Year to consist only of 4, or of but 3 Months, as Macrobius tells us in his Saturnalia, Lib. 1. The Carians and Acharanians, faith Justin, made their Year to consist of 6 Months, and reckoned but 15 Days to their Month. The Romans had three forts of Years : 1. That of Romulus, which contained but ten Months ; from whence the last Month of our Year retains the Name of December, as being the Tenth of his. This Year begun in March. 2. .Nutria Pompilius his Year; which had Romulus his gross Mistake corrected, and two more Months added to it, vi%. January and February ; and then it contained only 355 Days, or 12 Lunar Months. 3. The Year of Julius Cæsar, who discovering that there were 1 o Days more than Numa reckoned,made the Year 365 Days: and reserving the 6 Hours till every fourth Year, they then made another Day, which was added before the sixth of the Calends of March ; so that in this Fourth Year they accounted the 6th of the Calends of March twice ; Bis-sexto-calendars, whence came the Word Bijsextile or Leap-Year, as we call it; which hath 3 66 Days. This account is now used in England , and is the Julian or Old Stile. But because there was still found an Error in this Calculation, and that the Equinoxes did plainly, tho’ insensibly recede from the Points where Cæsar had six’d them; as also, that the Year was discovert! to want about 1 , Minutes of 36s Days aud 6 Hours ; which 11 Minutes will in 13 1 Years make the Equinoxes go back about a Day ; Pope Gregory XIII. to Reform (as he thought) this Error, ordered 1 o Days to be taken from the Year, to bring the Equinoxes that Year (which was 1582) to March 21, and Sept. 22, 23. Aud this is what is called the Gregorian Account or New Stile, as is used by the Popish Nations every where. The Great Tear, or the Annas Magnus, about 25000 or 26000 Years ; in which Time the Fix’d Stars will appear to come to the same Point again, exactly after one en tire Revolution.
